text_blocks.snippet: Common and serious side effects associated with Jardiance (empagliflozin) are tied to how the medication works by helping the kidneys remove extra sugar and fluid through urine.

list.snippet: Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Burning, urgency, frequency, pain, or cloudy urine.
Genital yeast infections: Vaginal yeast infections (itching, burning, thick white discharge) in women, or yeast infections around the penis and scrotum in men.
Increased urination: Going to the bathroom more often or needing to pee more frequently during the day or night.
Increased thirst: Dry mouth or a greater need to drink fluids.

text_blocks.snippet: Seek immediate medical attention or contact your healthcare provider right away if you experience signs of these severe reactions:

list.snippet: Dehydration: Dizziness, lightheadedness, feeling faint, weakness, or dark yellow urine—especially if you are older, take water pills (diuretics), or have kidney issues.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid in the blood, which can happen even if blood sugar is not very high. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual fatigue, trouble breathing, or a fruity odor on your breath.

Low blood sugar (Hypoglycemia): More common if Jardiance is taken alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas. Symptoms include shakiness, confusion, fast heart rate, and cold sweats.
Severe urinary tract or kidney infections: High fever, chills, lower back or side pain.

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier's gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineal (genital and rectal) area, causing severe pain, redness, swelling, and fever.
Lower limb amputations: Higher risk reported in patients with a history of amputation, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetic foot ulcers.
Serious allergic reactions: Hives, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, and throat causing difficulty breathing or swallowing.

text_blocks.snippet: For official safety details, patient guides, and prescribing information, you can review the Boehringer Ingelheim Jardiance Resource Page.
